text:
alex: Heads-up — planning to enable speculative decoding (flag: runtime.spec_decoding) in a canary tomorrow 10:00 PST. Need owners for rollback, perf/quality guardrails, and canary audience.

maya: scope? whole cluster or just a subset of hosts?

alex: start with 1% of traffic on the eastus pool (gpu-pool-eu1 still excluded). We'll only target the new v2 runtime nodes.

jonathan: watch out for flash-attn interplay — speculative decoding can change token stepping; we should ensure flash_attn_v2 isn't rolled simultaneously. Suggest disabling flash_attn_v2 for canary or pin to v1 kernel.

luis: KV cache behavior — speculative decoding may increase cache churn because of branchy prefixes. Recommend kv_cache_ttl=30s for canary, and enable cache metrics (hits/misses/evictions) at 1s granularity.

emily: SLO/alerts: add a smoke that fails if p50 gen latency regresses >30% or if error-rate >0.2% for 5m. Also add quality regression hook: run the short eval set every 10m and alert on >5% divergence.

alex: agreed. Owner list: alex (rollout), jonathan (kernel interactions), luis (cache), emily (SRE/alerts). Maya can coordinate canary audience.

maya: propose audience: 5 internal teams (devex, growth, sales-sim) + 1% production traffic (cross-traffic constrained to non-critical customer IDs). We have tag prefixes: dev-* and canary-cust-*.

jonathan: operational kill-switch: flag toggle + runtime check that falls back if failure pattern detected. Pseudo: `if (spec_decoding && (err_rate > 0.002 || latency_p50 > baseline*1.3)) { set_flag(runtime.spec_decoding,false) }`

alex: good. Add LaunchDarkly entry and a Launchdarkly-safe UUID so support can flip quickly.

launchbot: Created LD flag `runtime.spec_decoding` -> https://ld.redwood/runtime/spec_decoding. Default off, environments: staging, prod-canary, prod.

luis: small rollout steps: 0.5% -> 1% -> 5% with 30m observation at each step. We should capture per-model metrics (llama-3 vs gptx) since behaviour differs.

emily: also ensure logs include a `spec_decoding=true/false` field so the trace funneling works. Add a metric `spec_decoding_fallbacks` for how many times fallback executed.

alex: test checklist before canary:
- LD flag exists + kill switch in place
- metric dashboards created (latency, errors, cache evictions, eval divergence)
- canary audience configured in routing rules
- rollout automation script ready (`scripts/rollout_spec_decoding.sh`)
- postmortem owner assigned (jonathan)

maya: I'll create the routing rule and update the runbook.

jonathan: code snippet to toggle via internal flags API:
```
curl -X POST https://flags.internal/redwood/toggle \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $FLAGS_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"flag":"runtime.spec_decoding","enabled":true,"rollout":0.01,"meta":{"kernel":"v1-only","kv_ttl":30}}'
```

alex: perfect. After the first 1% succeed for 30m with no alerts, we bump to 5% and run the eval set. If eval divergence >5% we rollback immediately.

emily: SRE will attach an automated incident if alerts fire. I'll make a pareto of top failing prompts if quality regression triggers.

launchbot: Reminder: do not enable speculative decoding together with `runtime.flash_attn_v2` — LaunchDarkly target rule will enforce mutual exclusivity for prod-canary.

luis: one more ask — instrument CPU steal and p99 kernel stalls; speculative decoding sometimes causes scheduler jitter on older drivers.

alex: noted. All right — owners have tasks. We'll run the canary tomorrow 10:00 PST. Ping in thread when you flip the flag.

jonathan: will PR the small runtime guard that forces fallback when `spec_decoding_fallbacks` > 10 in 1m.

maya: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/spec_decoding_canary (I'll update with audience ids).

sre-bot: scheduled alerting policy `spec_decoding-canary` created. Channels: #eng-runtime, #oncall. Escalation: 5m to oncall.

alex: thanks everyone :thumbsup: Ping me directly if you want to test earlier in staging.

jonathan: once we clear canary, can we schedule a separate flash_attn_v2 canary window next week so they don't overlap?

alex: yes — separate window + different audience. We'll treat flash_attn_v2 as independent.

luis: noted, will monitor cache metrics during canary and post a short summary in this thread after 2h.

maya: I'll flip the routing rules and post the final canary audience here when done.

launchbot: LD flag `runtime.spec_decoding` set to ON for prod-canary @ 1752346005 (audit id: ld-audit-8802).
